items.question: Does converting JPG to PNG improve image quality?
items.answer: No. While PNG is a lossless format, converting an existing JPG cannot restore compression artifacts or visual details that JPEG lossy compression already discarded.

items.question: Why are converted PNG files often larger than the original JPG?
items.answer: PNG uses lossless DEFLATE compression which preserves exact pixel color values, whereas JPEG uses lossy discrete cosine transform. Consequently, converted PNG files are almost always larger.

items.question: Can I convert multiple JPGs and download them as a ZIP archive?
items.answer: Yes. You can select multiple images to convert them in batch, downloading them individually or bundled together in a ZIP file.

items.question: Are my images uploaded to any remote server?
items.answer: No. The conversion is performed locally via your browser HTML5 Canvas. No image data is ever uploaded or transmitted.

items.question: Can I convert other formats to PNG?
items.answer: Yes. The converter accepts JPG, JPEG, WebP, and BMP files and converts them all into standard lossless PNG.

items.question: How does the PNG format compress image data?
items.answer: PNG uses LZ77-derived DEFLATE compression paired with predictive horizontal/vertical byte filters to pack repeated color runs without discarding data.

items.question: Does converting JPG to PNG add a transparent background?
items.answer: Converting JPG creates an opaque PNG since JPEGs contain no alpha channel. To add transparency, pixels must be edited or keyed out separately.

items.question: When is PNG preferred over JPG for graphics?
items.answer: PNG is ideal for digital illustrations, screenshots, UI diagrams, and typography where sharp edge definitions and color consistency are essential.
